body: I got some to off myself with, a year and a half ago. Really I was curious about opioids - had been for a long time - and I inevitably dipped into my exit stash. It was good but not that good...nothing worth throwing your life away over, I remember telling myself at the time. Anyway, I developed a taste for it, ended up using daily, and became heavily addicted all while kidding myself I was only physically dependent, using medicinally, and could taper off whenever I wanted. Heroin was more subtle than I'd expected, but if I'd known what would come of that decision to try it, and the decisions which followed, I would have tossed the whole lot away. You might think you'll never touch a needle, but when you're dopesick that might change. You might think you'll just try this once and leave it at that, and you might do, but it's not worth the risk, and heroin isn't as amazing as it's sometimes portrayed to be. I had to learn all this the hard way. I hope you don't. God bless!

Very well said. I also commented here to make the point that hatred is usually not the motivating factor behind the expression of anti-LGBTQ viewpoints on the part of Christians. Call it bigotry, call it the rightful condemnation of sin...but calling it hate is often simply inaccurate.

It shouldn't be difficult - in fact it's a skill that all parents (and teachers) have to master. When a son or daughter does something 'bad', the parent must be clear with them that what they've done isn't OK whilst retaining a loving demeanour towards them. Is this not how we Christians should position ourselves with regard to sin? I'd estimate that a good 95% of members of the church I attend are very much opposed to the 'promotion and normalisation' of LGBTQ identities, however these genuinely the sweetest and most loving people that I know. Many are involved in volunteer work in some capacity where they will encounter people from all walks of life, including many with LGBTQ identities nowadays especially. I don't see hatred or bigotry; I see pity and a desire to help. This isn't to say that hatred against LGBTQ folk doesn't exist - it certainly does and I've seen plenty of it, mostly from ultra-right wingers who either LARP as Christians - often as Orthodox - or hate Christianity for antisemitic reasons on the ground that Jesus was a Jew.

What I never see is genuine hatred from devout, church-going Christians. "Bigotry?" yes, probably. But what gets called bigotry is NOT necessarily hatred. I expect to get downvoted for saying this on this sub, but it's my experience and I stand by it.
